opportunities.saving_basis: measured 3.769 ms (C-6651; C-7968 minus C-6773 minus C-1508 gives a consistent 3.744). Ideal 1.361 ms.

cards.note: only states the duplicate wq_a/wkv_a quantization; sharing it removes one quantize+swizzle but not the norm re-read

opportunities.notes: C-6651's ideal (214 MB/inst) overcounts bytes; recomputed. If O-19 is adopted, the bf16 normed write could also be dropped (~0.52 ms more), but no card proposes that.

opportunities.title: MoE output combine: top-k scale_and_sum + shared-expert add + residual add

opportunities.title: q RoPE applied in the wq_b GEMM epilogue
opportunities.ops_summary: forward / layers.*.attention torchtitan.fused_mla_q_rope (out-of-place full q copy) folded into layers.*.attention.wq_b _scaled_mm_v2 (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: removes the q rope kernel (measured 3.589 ms, C-7365). wq_b GEMM is compute-bound (309 GFLOP -> 85.5 us vs 35.8 us of bytes), so the epilogue rotation adds ~0. C-1332's 3.979 also counts the GEMM's own gap to peak (~0.39 ms), which fusion does not remove.
opportunities.notes: cuBLAS nvjet has no custom epilogue; needs a CUTLASS/CuTe MXFP8 GEMM.

opportunities.title: MLA K assembly (k_nope copy + rotated k_pe broadcast) in the wkv_b GEMM epilogue
opportunities.ops_summary: forward / layers.*.attention.inner_attention torchtitan.fused_mla_k_rope folded into .wkv_b _scaled_mm_v2 (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: k rope kernel measured 3.094 ms (C-5475). wkv_b GEMM is memory-bound (287.9 MB -> 41.6 us); writing K [4096,128,192] + V separately instead of kv adds 67.1 MB (+k_pe 0.5) -> +9.77 us per layer. Saving (50.72 - 9.77) x 61.
opportunities.notes: C-7582's fused ideal (490.8 MB) keeps the full kv write and its gap includes the GEMM's own inefficiency (~1.1 ms); recomputed. V stops being a free view.

opportunities.title: RoPE position bound check done once per step instead of per layer
opportunities.ops_summary: forward / layers.*.attention le + all + _assert_async on the same positions tensor (61 x 3 kernels)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 0.459 ms (C-8742); replacement ideal ~0 (537 bytes).
opportunities.notes: Cross-layer dedupe rather than a fusion of different ops; verified positions is the same tensor for every layer (fused_mla.py forward, rope.py _maybe_check_max_pos).

opportunities.title: MoE router forward in one row-wise kernel (sigmoid, bias, group top-k, top-8, gather/normalize, routing map, counts)

Ideal: logits fp32 4.19 MB in; scores 4.19, map 1.05, ids/weights 0.39 out = 9.8 MB -> 1.42 us x58 = 0.082 ms.
opportunities.notes: Three torch.topk calls (~72 us each) dominate. Must reproduce topk tie-breaking/order. A real kernel will be launch/latency bound (~10 us), still ~95% of the gap.

opportunities.title: Dist-MoE routing metadata / GEMM-plan kernels and padding glue (forward and backward)

cards.note: backward plan folded into the copy
folds the two padding masked_fills into the router kernel

opportunities.title: Dist-MoE activation save/restore copies (drop the redundant activation-buffer copy)

opportunities.saving_basis: measured 3.321 ms (C-8100, 3 copies of 58.7 MB). Ideal keeps the forward and backward symmetric-buffer copies (2 x 117.4 MB) and aliases the activation save to the resident ffn_norm output: 33.9 us x58 = 1.968 ms.

cards.note: reads x once for both forward copies but still writes the activation copy
only brings the backward copy to roofline (per-layer buffers alternative not costed)

opportunities.title: Dist-MoE grouped-GEMM prepare kernels folded into the GEMM prologue
opportunities.ops_summary: forward + backward / routed_experts cute *_prepare_* kernels before each fprop/dgrad/wgrad grouped GEMM (2 fwd + ~6 bwd per layer, 58 layers)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 2.033 ms (C-8973); prologue cost ~0 (metadata only).
opportunities.notes: Unverifiable from the repo (Dist-MoE kernels are external); if a prepare kernel publishes state to peers before the dispatch GEMM starts, folding it needs an in-kernel cross-rank ordering and the saving shrinks.

opportunities.title: Emit the colwise MXFP8 copy of bf16-saved linear inputs in the forward quantize (no backward requantize)
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.*.attention.{wq_a,wkv_a,wq_b,wo}, feed_forward.(shared_experts.)w13, lm_head colwise mxfp8_quantize + swizzle of the saved bf16 input; replaced by a colwise output of the forward quantizer (62)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 6.302 ms (C-9441; C-2076 reports 7.112 including ~0.8 ms beyond the backward requant, used the smaller). Ideal = extra colwise writes in forward (input read is shared): per layer fp8 29.36 (attention_norm out, shared by wq_a/wkv_a) + 29.36 (ffn_norm out) + 6.29 (q_norm out) + 67.11 (O) + scales 4.13 = 136.25 MB; lm_head 30.3 MB -> 1.205 ms.
opportunities.notes: Changes the saved-activation format: saves memory for attention_norm/q_norm/lm_head inputs, costs ~4 GB extra for O and ffn_norm output whose bf16 stays alive for FA backward / router gate. The recipe keeps bf16 for these on purpose.

opportunities.title: Horizontal GEMM fusion of wq_a and wkv_a (forward N-concat, dgrad K-concat)
opportunities.ops_summary: forward + backward / layers.*.attention.wq_a and .wkv_a _scaled_mm_v2 fprop and dgrad (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 5.873 ms (C-5923; C-9619 5.893). Fused ideal: N=2112 fprop and K=2112 dgrad, each 124 GFLOP -> 34.3 us at MXFP8 peak (bytes 62-83 MB, 9-12 us): 68.6 us x61 = 4.185 ms.
opportunities.notes: The saving is GEMM efficiency (N=576 GEMM runs at half its roofline); a merged GEMM will not reach peak, so this is an upper bound. Forward concat is bitwise; the K-concat dgrad changes accumulation order. Needs a stacked parameter or grouped GEMM.

opportunities.title: Cross: merged wq_a/wkv_a dgrad removes the second partial-gradient read in attention_norm backward
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.*.attention.wq_a add (dX sum) absorbed by the K-concat dgrad (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: extra over O-20 + O-28: the fused attention_norm-backward kernel reads one dX instead of two (58.72 MB) -> 8.48 us x61.

cards.note: states the add in the norm backward disappears

opportunities.notes: Only with the non-bitwise K-concat dgrad; a grouped GEMM with a fused bf16 add keeps the read.

opportunities.title: Fused cross-entropy (forward keeps LSE; backward writes MXFP8 dlogits for lm_head)
opportunities.ops_summary: forward / loss _to_copy fp32, _log_softmax, nll_loss_forward, div, ones_like; backward / nll_loss_backward, _log_softmax_backward_data, _to_copy bf16, div; lm_head dY mxfp8_quantize + swizzles (1)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 4.193 ms (both cards). Ideal two-kernel form: read bf16 logits [4096,129280] (1059 MB) in forward and again in backward, write fp8 rowwise+colwise 1059 MB + scales 33 MB = 3210 MB -> 0.464 ms.
opportunities.notes: Removes the 2.1 GB fp32 copies and saved log_softmax. Crosses the loss/model boundary and lm_head's MXFP8 autograd Function.

opportunities.title: Cross-entropy forward and backward in a single pass over the logits
opportunities.ops_summary: same ops as O-22; the backward is computed in the forward kernel (1)
opportunities.saving_basis: extra over O-22: logits are read once instead of twice (1059 MB) -> 0.153 ms (fused ideal 0.311 ms).

opportunities.title: Router + aux-loss backward to the gate-logit gradient in one row-wise kernel
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.3-60.feed_forward.routed_experts masked_fill; router mul/div/sum/neg/gather_backward (sort-based scatter_add)/add_/sigmoid_backward; router.aux_loss where/sgn/gt/mul/div/sum/... (58)

opportunities.notes: Top-k ids are unique per row, so the deterministic sort-based scatter_add becomes a direct store with identical bits.

opportunities.title: HiMidLo split of the gate-logit gradient written directly into the stacked bf16 GEMM operand
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.3-60.feed_forward.router.gate _to_copy, __lshift__, sub (x2), cat -> [4096,768] (58)

opportunities.title: Router gate weight-gradient: three wgrad GEMMs accumulated in one GEMM, no stacked-weight copy
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.3-60.feed_forward.router.gate cat (weight x3), mm x3 (wgrad), add_ x2, _to_copy (58)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 3.366 ms (C-9194). Fused ideal: one bf16 GEMM computing the three [256,7168] products while reading x once, 45.1 GFLOP -> 23.4 us x58 = 1.356 ms.

cards.note: GEMM beta=1 accumulation removes the add_/cast kernels but keeps three GEMMs each reading x

Ideal 7.033 ms.

opportunities.title: w2 dY MXFP8 quantize fused into a kernel that already holds dy
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.*.feed_forward.(shared_experts.)w2 dY mxfp8_quantize + 2 swizzles (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 1.594 ms = C-1047 (7.476) minus C-7467 (5.882); C-1543 minus C-4163 gives 1.799, used the smaller. Ideal: only the fp8 rowwise+colwise writes (60.6 MB -> 8.75 us) x61 = 0.534 ms; dy is read by the producer (attention_norm backward, C-1047) or by broadcast_and_scale (C-1543).

cards.note: consumer-side; the 3 dense layers keep a standalone quantize

opportunities.title: Routed-expert backward broadcast_and_scale folded into the expert GEMMs (no [T,K,D] dx materialisation)
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.3-60.feed_forward.routed_experts triton broadcast_and_scale (dx = dy*score, dscore = <dy,x>) (58)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 9.704 ms (C-4163). Ideal: dy read by the recompute-fprop epilogue (dscore) and by the dgrad operand load (2 x 58.72 MB) -> 17.0 us x58 = 0.986 ms (both GEMMs are compute-bound, so this is an upper bound on the added cost).

cards.note: keeps broadcast_and_scale, only brings it to roofline (998.5 MB per layer)

opportunities.notes: Dist-MoE owns the kernels; dscore is a D=7168 reduction across N-tiles (ordered partials needed); in real EP the expert rank needs the source token's dy over symmetric memory; dx must be quantized in the prologue. Fake-PG GEMM times are not representative.

opportunities.title: Flash-attention backward preprocess (rowsum(dO*O), dQaccum zero) in the wo dgrad GEMM epilogue
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / layers.*.attention.wo dgrad _scaled_mm_v2 + preprocess kernels inside torch_attn._varlen_attn_backward (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 22.876 ms GEMM + preprocess (C-5659). wo dgrad is compute-bound: 962 GFLOP -> 266.1 us; the epilogue's extra O read (134 MB) and dQaccum zeroing (403 MB) fit under it. Fused ideal 16.232 ms.
opportunities.notes: Upper bound: the saving also absorbs the GEMM's own gap to peak, which cannot be separated from the card's numbers (at most ~0.7 ms, since the preprocess alone needs >= 97 us per layer). cuBLAS has no custom epilogue; FA owns the dpsum layout.

opportunities.title: q RoPE backward + wq_b dY MXFP8 quantize in one pass

opportunities.saving_basis: measured 5.994 ms (C-7143). Ideal: read dq bf16 201.3 MB, write fp8 x2 201.3 + scales 6.3 = 408.9 MB -> 59.1 us x61 = 3.604 ms.

opportunities.title: Cross: produce wq_b's MXFP8 dY straight from flash-attention's fp32 dQ accumulator (replaces the dQ postprocess)

opportunities.notes: Needs a hook into the attention backward to replace its postprocess (attention epilogue); arithmetic is pointwise so bitwise is achievable (round to bf16 first). C-7143 mentions this only as a further step.

opportunities.title: FSDP backward re-unshard all-gather copy-in (same cast + pack)
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / per-block fp32 shard casts + clone + _foreach_copy_ before the backward all-gather (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: only C-7411 reports it (its backward half ~6.55 ms). Measured taken as the forward per-block cost of the smaller forward report (C-2650: 4.894 x 61/62 = 4.815 ms) for consistency with O-41. Ideal 2.266 ms.
opportunities.notes: Parameters do not change between forward and backward, so caching the bf16 shard would remove it entirely (memory cost). Using C-7411's own figure the saving would be ~4.3 ms.

opportunities.title: FSDP forward all-gather copy-out fused with MXFP8 weight quantization
opportunities.ops_summary: forward / split_with_sizes_copy of the gathered bucket, w13 dim-1 reassembly cat, torchao 32x32 weight quantize, dist_moe.prepare_mxfp8_weight (blocks + norm/lm_head group)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 35.204 ms (C-7051; C-1888's forward half is larger because it also counts the temp->persistent copy_ and clone, recorded in O-45). Fused ideal: read the gathered bf16 buffer once and write fp8 qdata + scales (+bf16 router/norm weights): MoE block 821 + 412 MB = 1233 MB -> 178.1 us x58, dense block 1754 MB -> 253.5 us x3, norm/lm_head 2782 MB -> 401.9 us. Ideal 11.494 ms.
opportunities.notes: Both cards' ideals are too high (2.1 and 3.0 GB/inst): they keep most of today's traffic. One qdata allocation serves fprop and dgrad (tensor.py), so 1 byte/element.

opportunities.title: FSDP backward re-unshard copy-out fused with MXFP8 weight quantization
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / same copy-out + quantize ops for the backward all-gather of each block (61)
opportunities.saving_basis: only C-1888 covers it. Measured taken as the forward per-block cost of C-7051 scaled to the 61 blocks (35.204 x 11.092/11.494 = 33.97 ms); the rest of C-1888's 92.83 ms is assigned to O-45. Ideal 11.092 ms.
opportunities.notes: Default reshard_after_forward (no PP) re-gathers in backward. Keeping the MXFP8 operands from forward removes this half entirely at ~23 GB of memory.

opportunities.title: Quantize straight into the persistent MXFP8 operand storage (drop the temp -> persistent copy_ and the dim-1 clone)
opportunities.ops_summary: forward + backward / _build_operands copy_ refill of qdata/scales and contiguous clone of dim-1-sharded w13 (123)
opportunities.saving_basis: C-1888's 92.828 ms minus the copy-out/quantize parts assigned to O-43/O-44 (35.204 + 33.973) = 23.65 ms (~190 us per block, consistent with 932 MB of copy_ + clone traffic per MoE block). Fused ideal 0 (the O-43/O-44 kernels write the persistent buffers).
opportunities.notes: Verified the copy_ refill in torchtitan/quantization/mxfp8/tensor.py _build_operands; C-7051 does not list these ops. Derived split, so moderate uncertainty.

opportunities.title: FSDP reduce-scatter copy-in in one pass (w13 dim-1 shard interleave folded into the pack)
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / per-block w13 grad interleave cat (256 chunks) + _chunk_cat / bucketing._pre_bucket_reduce_scatter into the RS input (62)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 39.701 ms (C-8089, 62 groups; C-4715's 40.397 also includes the embedding group, moved to O-39). Ideal: read every bf16 grad once and write the RS buffer once: MoE block 1642 MB -> 237 us x58, dense 2339 MB x3, norm/lm_head 3707 MB -> 15.311 ms.
opportunities.notes: C-8089's ideal (22.94 ms) is too high. Most of the gap is chunk_cat running well below roofline plus the strided 256-input cat; needs per-tensor shard-dim support in fsdp::chunk_cat.

opportunities.title: Reduce-scatter output cast to fp32 written directly into param.grad (no per-parameter casts + clone)
opportunities.ops_summary: backward / per-parameter bf16 -> fp32 _to_copy after each reduce-scatter (848) + param.grad clone/copy_ (848) (63)
opportunities.saving_basis: measured 8.521 ms (C-9655). Ideal: one multi-tensor cast per bucket, read bf16 + write fp32 (269.7 MB per MoE block) -> 2.273 ms.
opportunities.notes: The clone runs in the runtime's gradient hand-off after the program, at the edge of the backward scope; counted because it is gradient glue, not optimizer math.
